Terms of use Effective November 19, 2026. CommuteScout is informational only. Data can be delayed, incomplete, or wrong. Always verify with your state's official 511 service or DOT map (for California, quickmap.dot.ca.gov ) before you drive, and never rely on this service for evacuation or any emergency decision. If you are in danger, call 911. What this is A free, independent project that displays public road data from state and federal sources across the country - CHP, Caltrans, other state transportation agencies, and national wildfire and weather feeds - plus routing, an AI assistant, watch-area alerts, the CommuteScout Drive navigation apps for iPhone and Android, and an MCP server and REST API. Coverage varies by state and the map says so where it is missing. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by any government agency. Names of data sources are used to describe where data comes from, nothing more. Using it Drive safely. Set your route before you start, and don't look at or touch the screen while the vehicle is moving; let the Drive app's voice guidance and alerts do the talking, or have a passenger handle it. Obey traffic laws, road signs, and officials on the scene: they win over anything the app or map says, including a route that tells you to turn where you shouldn't. Routes, drive times, and alerts are estimates built from public feeds and can be wrong or out of date. They are not a substitute for your state's official 511 or DOT information. Don't abuse it: no scraping at volumes that degrade it for others, no attempts to bypass rate limits or access controls, no using the assistant for anything other than road questions. API keys belong to your account. Keep them secret, and don't put one in a web page or app that others can read. Request limits apply per account, shared by all of its keys, and per address without a key; we can change limits and revoke keys that are abused. Plugins can be run by people other than us. What a plugin shows is its operator's, not ours, and reports you post go to the plugins you have switched on as the privacy policy describes. Watch-area accounts are an invite-gated trial. We can approve, limit, or revoke access at any time. Areas are checked about every five minutes, and alert delivery is best effort - alerts can be late, missed, or wrong. Ending access We can suspend or end access for anyone who violates these terms or abuses the service, with or without notice. You can stop using the service whenever you like. No warranty, limited liability The service is provided as is, without warranties of any kind, express or implied, including fitness for a particular purpose. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the operator is not liable for any damages arising from use of the service or reliance on its data, including decisions made based on alerts, maps, routes, or assistant answers. That limit covers indirect, incidental, consequential, special, and punitive damages alike, along with any lost data, profits, or time, even if we were warned they were possible. Road conditions are verified by official sources, not by us; your driving decisions are yours. The code The software is open source under the MIT license at github.com/nicglazkov/commutescout . These terms cover this hosted instance, not the code - you are welcome to run your own.
